$comment: P69 L2 (lane lm): five parenthesised call chains, 30 levels each — calls inside parentheses, a cast to a typedef around each call, a function-pointer OBJECT called through parentheses, a cast to a function-pointer TYPE as the callee, and an object shadowing a typedef called through parentheses. Each `(` opens a speculation (cast, compound literal or parenthesised expression) the parser must decide, and every chain but the first asks the binder sketch at every level. While a level's failed probe was re-run under every enclosing level's retry the parse grew x1.62 per level (MEASURED 2026-10-20, macos-arm64-debug: 9245 ms at 24 levels; INFERRED ~100 s per chain at 30); the failed-probe memo and the triage's base asked when the probe opens its type make it linear (the cost itself is pinned by ParserSpeculationRefusalCost.EveryParenthesisedChainCostsWorkLinearInItsDepth, on token work). gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 build THIS file at -std=gnu2x and -std=gnu17, -O0 and -O2, and at -std=c2x -pedantic-errors, and it exits 42 (MEASURED 2026-10-21, WSL). Exit 42, or the number of the first chain that answers wrong. The release arm folds the same chains through the optimizer.
